contributorNote: Swahili (Kiswahili: Kiunguja, Kimvita, Kiamu, Kitikuu, Kipate, Kingozi) vocabulary compiled from Rev. Dr. J. L. Krapf (1850, 1882), Bishop Edward Steere (1870, 1894, 1918), Rev. W. E. Taylor (1891), George W. Bateman (1901), A. C. Madan (1902, 1903, 1905, 1917 "English-Swahili Vocabulary", SPCK London, pp. 1–56 [PDF pp. 1–72]), Hildegarde Hinde (1904), Mrs. F. Burt (1910), Capt. C. H. Stigand (1915), Mervyn W. H. Beech (1918), Prof. Alice Werner (1918, 1919, 1933), Sir Harry H. Johnston (1919), Deo Ngonyani & Nancy Ngowa (2016), Mohamed Mwamzandi (2022), and John Goldsmith & Fidèle Mpiranya (2022). Expanded and cross-verified with Commercially Permissive Datasets (Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, KenPOS, KenTrans, KenSwQuAD, KenSpeech Lexicon, CC-BY-4.0), Thiomi (CC-BY-4.0), Google SMOL/GATITOS (CC-BY-4.0), LughaGen (CC-BY-SA-4.0), Common Voice 25.0 (CC0-1.0), CLDF WOLD & Tsammalex (CC-BY-4.0), Kaikki.org (CC-BY-SA-4.0), Language Science Press (2016/2019/2022, CC-BY-4.0)).

entries.english: To touch by handling anything gently, or by putting only the fingers upon a thing

entries.english: To speak or make a noise during sleep, to cry out in sleep, to have the nightmare
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To shut to, to close (door without fastening), press (used of extracting vegetab)

entries.english: To collect together for picking up, scoop up, gather up (used in a collective se)
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt, Swahili Grammar and Vocabulary (SPCK London, 1910 — Public Domain) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To tear, rend, tatter, tear asunder ; (Ku)rarua-rarua (v. red.), to tear to pieces

entries.english: To groan like a woman in travail or like a person in severe sickness, or to strain

entries.english: To to receive for another, to transmit, to take from one and deliver it to a third

entries.english: To cough on purpose to attract the observation of him with whom one wishes to speak
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To go shares, take part in, communicate ; (Ku)sharikana, to participate, communicate

entries.english: To pursue a thing, by hiding oneself and by bending and stooping
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To be disentangled, unravelled, disintegrated, torn into tatters
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt, Swahili Grammar and Vocabulary (SPCK London, 1910 — Public Domain) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To suspect one, to doubt of his real intention, to revile, insult
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To cause to abhor (hence to be outrageous, abhorrent, abominable)
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. c.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To (or at) their house, to (or at) them, equivalent to their home
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt, Swahili Grammar and Vocabulary (SPCK London, 1910 — Public Domain) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To be able, can (used negatively for disability through sickness)
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt, Swahili Grammar and Vocabulary (SPCK London, 1910 — Public Domain) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To vex or upbraid one about a matter which has before been refused
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To pronounce blessing (auctioneer) on thing knocked down to bidder
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. prep.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To (or at) their house, to (or at) them, equivalent to their home.
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [poss. pro.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To exercise self-control, be temperate, moderate, restrain one’s self
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. ref.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To be conducive, to be of use, to serve, to be good for, to be smooth
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To knock at the door, to announce oneself at a house by calling hodi !
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. intr.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To become accustomed to, acquire the habit of, get used to, become tame
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt, Swahili Grammar and Vocabulary (SPCK London, 1910 — Public Domain) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To hesitate, to be in suspense or doubt, to be doubtful, to be perplexed
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. intr.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To commit a crime, transgress, rebel, swerve from right course of action
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. tr. and intr.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To mingle one language with another, to jumble together different languages
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To have the quality of being prospered or of being in a prosperous condition
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To strip (a bed) (in contradistinction to tandika, making a bed) and roll up
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt, Swahili Grammar and Vocabulary (SPCK London, 1910 — Public Domain) • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To rebuke, to reprove, to admonish, to snub one, to use one roughly, to scold
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To be obtainable, procurable ; (Ku)patikana ni, to meet with, have happen to one
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. n.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To be at the expense for, to spend property for the accomplishment of a certain purpose
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To scratch the skin so that blood flows, to hurt, injure, or wound one's-self by rubbing
entries.context: Rev. Dr. L. Krapf (1882) A Dictionary of the Suahili Language • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To strip (a bed) (in contradistinction to tandika, making a bed) and roll up the bedding
entries.context: Mrs. F. Burt (1910) — Mombasa (Kimvita) Vocabulary [v. sub.] • Cross-verified with Kencorpus (KenCorpus_text, CC-BY-4.0)

entries.english: To trouble, annoy, persecute, harass, molest ; Likakuudhi hata Ku-Kuua, It mortified you
